prompt.context: Our client is a supplier to the microwavable popcorn industry. They supply popcorn makers (e.g., Act II, Orville Redenbacher's) with the grease-resistant paper used to package popcorn kernels in a variety of serving sizes. In this industry, the quality of the paper is determined by placing a bag of freshly microwaved popcorn on a napkin and measuring the amount of grease that seeps through the paper packaging and is absorbed by the napkin. The R&D department of our client recently developed a new type of paper that doubles the performance of the paper. A new coating is applied that virtually eliminates any seepage of grease in the napkin test.
prompt.question: Should our client introduce this new product into the market?

clarifying_info.q: What is the overall market size?
clarifying_info.a: Overall volume in the market is 100 million sheets of grease-resistant paper per year.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the competitors in this market?
clarifying_info.a: There are 4 players who supply paper in this market. Our client holds the largest market share (50%), with the rest of the market share split evenly among the other 3 competitors. Market share for all players has been stable over the last decade.

clarifying_info.q: How did our client achieve its larger market share?
clarifying_info.a: They were the first mover into the market.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any difference between the paper supplied by our client and competitors?
clarifying_info.a: All players have been producing and supplying essentially the same type and quality of paper since microwavable popcorn was introduced.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a history of innovations in the grease-resistant paper market?
clarifying_info.a: All players have been producing and supplying essentially the same type and quality of paper since microwavable popcorn was introduced.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any threat of the popcorn makers vertically integrating?
clarifying_info.a: Not really. Popcorn makers differentiate on brand and are not really interested in entering production of what is essentially a commodity product.

clarifying_info.q: Is there pricing pressure evident in this market?
clarifying_info.a: Prices have been relatively stable over the last decade, though recently there has been some increasing pressure as the retail price for microwavable popcorn has been dropping.

clarifying_info.q: Will our client's customers be able to differentiate themselves by using the new paper?
clarifying_info.a: They have not had direct conversations with the popcorn makers. They did however run some initial focus groups with end-customers (buyers of popcorn), and found the amount of grease that seeps through paper is not a concern for buyers and introducing the new paper will not necessarily sway consumers' buying decisions.

clarifying_info.q: Will producing the new paper require a large capital investment?
clarifying_info.a: The cost of setting up the new production will be minimal.

clarifying_info.q: Will the new paper increase our client's raw material costs?
clarifying_info.a: It currently costs our client $0.10 to produce each sheet of paper. The chemicals in the coating of the new paper increase the cost of a sheet by 20% to $0.12.

clarifying_info.q: Will popcorn makers incur any additional costs to accommodate the new paper in their production process?
clarifying_info.a: They will not incur any extra costs. In fact, they will actually be able to save money. The old paper required popcorn makers to glue two sheets of paper together before packaging to achieve the desired grease resistance. The new paper allows popcorn makers to eliminate this step, which previously added $0.12 to their total packaging costs. Under the old system: 2 sheets needed at $0.20 each plus $0.12 to glue = $0.52 total. Under the new system: 1 sheet needed, no gluing required, total cost = price of 1 new sheet.

framework: Understand the supply chain and market context: who buys the paper, how it is used, and the competitive dynamics of the commodity paper market
Assess whether the new paper creates value for the direct customer (popcorn makers) and the end consumer: does it enable differentiation or reduce costs?
Analyze the volume impact: because the new paper eliminates the need to double-layer sheets, switching to the new product halves the number of sheets purchased per unit of popcorn

Develop a pricing strategy: determine a price for the new sheet that keeps popcorn makers' total packaging costs at or below the current level while maintaining or improving our client's profitability
Consider competitive and strategic implications: patent protection, sales/marketing approach, pre-selling the innovation to clients, and the risk that competitors replicate the technology

questions.prompt: Walk through the supply chain impact of introducing the new paper. What happens to our client's volume?
questions.guidance: The key insight is that the new paper is superior enough that popcorn makers only need 1 sheet instead of 2. If our client maintains the same 50% market share, they will sell 50 million sheets instead of the current 100 million sheets sold industry-wide (50M attributed to our client). In other words, volume attributable to our client drops from 50 million to 25 million sheets — a 50% reduction. Any pricing strategy must account for this volume decline.

math.setup: Current market: 100M sheets/year total. Client market share: 50%. Current client volume: 50M sheets/year. New paper: 1 sheet replaces 2, so total industry sheets needed = 50M. Client volume at same market share = 25M sheets/year.
steps: New industry volume needed = 100M / 2 = 50M sheets (since 1 new sheet replaces 2 old sheets)
New client volume at 50% share = 50M x 50% = 25M sheets
math.answer: Introducing the new paper at the same market share reduces our client's volume by 50%, from 50 million to 25 million sheets per year.

questions.prompt: What price should our client charge for the new paper to maintain its current profitability? Use the packaging cost table as a guide.
questions.guidance: The candidate must set up a pricing equation that preserves both the client's margin and the popcorn makers' total packaging costs. Popcorn makers currently spend $0.52 per package (2 sheets at $0.20 each + $0.12 glue). If the new paper is priced at $0.52 per sheet, popcorn makers break even ($0.52 for 1 sheet, $0 gluing = $0.52 total). At $0.52, the client earns $0.52 - $0.12 (production cost) = $0.40 margin per sheet. To match current total profit: current profit = 50M sheets x ($0.20 - $0.10) = $5M/year. New profit at $0.52 = 25M sheets x ($0.52 - $0.12) = $10M/year. Thus $0.52 not only maintains profitability but doubles it. A superior answer identifies a range: any price up to $0.52 is acceptable to popcorn makers (they pay no more than today), and any price above $0.20 is better for our client than today. The sweet spot is pricing between $0.20 and $0.52.

math.setup: Old packaging cost per package for popcorn makers = 2 sheets x $0.20 + $0.12 glue = $0.52. New packaging cost = 1 sheet x (new price) + $0 gluing. For popcorn makers to break even, new price <= $0.52. Client production cost for new sheet = $0.12.
steps: Current annual client profit = 50M sheets x $0.10 = $5M
Break-even price for popcorn makers = $0.52 (one new sheet replaces two old sheets plus gluing)
New annual client profit at $0.52 = 25M x $0.40 = $10M
Minimum price to maintain current $5M profit = solve: 25M x (P - $0.12) = $5M => P - $0.12 = $0.20 => P = $0.32
Acceptable pricing range for popcorn makers: any price up to $0.52 (they save money or break even)
Optimal price range: $0.32 (maintains current profit) to $0.52 (doubles profit, popcorn makers break even)
math.answer: To maintain current profitability, the client must charge at least $0.32 per new sheet. At $0.52, popcorn makers pay no more than today and the client doubles its profit to $10M/year. The recommended price range is $0.32 to $0.52.

brainstorming.prompt: What additional steps should our client take to capitalize on this innovation?

categories.name: Intellectual Property
ideas: File a patent on the new coating technology to prevent competitors from replicating it
Explore trade secret protections for the manufacturing process

categories.name: Sales and Customer Management
ideas: Pre-sell the innovation to popcorn makers before launch to get buy-in and avoid sticker shock on the higher per-sheet price
Frame the value proposition around total packaging cost savings and production simplification, not just paper performance
Negotiate long-term supply contracts with popcorn makers to lock in volume at the new price

categories.name: Pricing Strategy
ideas: Adopt value-based pricing tied to the cost savings delivered to popcorn makers
Consider tiered pricing or volume discounts to capture market share from competitors
Price below $0.52 to make the value proposition obvious and drive adoption quickly

categories.name: Market Share Expansion
ideas: Use the cost advantage to win share from the 3 competitors who still require double-sheeting
Target popcorn makers currently using competitor paper first, since they have the highest switching incentive

categories.name: Risk Mitigation
ideas: Assess how quickly competitors could develop a similar coating
Plan a rapid rollout to establish relationships before competitors catch up
Evaluate whether the 20% cost increase in raw materials is stable or subject to supply chain volatility

recommendation: Our client should introduce the new paper, but only after pre-selling the innovation to popcorn makers and securing IP protection

The recommended price is in the range of $0.32 to $0.52 per sheet: this delivers cost savings or cost neutrality for popcorn makers while maintaining or significantly improving our client's profitability (current profit $5M/year; profit at $0.52 = $10M/year)
The rationale for introduction is cost reduction for popcorn makers (not consumer demand creation), which must be the core of the sales pitch
risks: Popcorn makers may perceive the higher per-sheet price ($0.32-$0.52 vs. $0.20) as a price increase without understanding the total-cost benefit — careful pre-selling is essential
Competitors could develop similar coating technology and erode the pricing power if the innovation is not patent-protected
If popcorn makers delay adoption, our client may see a period of reduced volume without the compensating margin improvement
next_steps: Immediately file for patent protection on the coating technology
Initiate conversations with key popcorn maker customers to present total packaging cost analysis
Develop a phased rollout plan with pricing anchored to demonstrated cost savings
Monitor competitor R&D activity and be prepared to accelerate commercialization if needed
